case_name: D. S. Reddy v Chancellor, Osmania University and Others
facts: The Osmania University was established in 1918 and the administration of the University was then governed by a Charter of His Exalted Highness, the Nizam of Hyderabad, promulgated in 1947.
With effect from November 1, 1956, the State of Hyderabad ceased to exist, and the Telengana region of that State became part of Andhra Pradesh.
The Osmania University Act, 1959 was passed by the Andhra Pradesh Legislature to amend and consolidate the law relating to the Osmania University.
In 1965, certain amendments were sought to be introduced in the Act by providing for removal of the Vice-Chancellor, by the Chancellor, from office under certain circumstances.
The Osmania University (Amendment) Act, 1966 was passed by the Andhra Pradesh Legislature amending the Osmania University Act of 1959 in certain particulars.
The Osmania University (Second Amendment) Act, 1966 was again passed by the Andhra Pradesh Legislature amending the Osmania University Act of 1959 in certain particulars.
issues: Whether the provision in s.13A of the Osmania University Act, 1959 is unconstitutional and void
Whether the Vice-Chancellor can be removed from office without giving him an opportunity to show cause against such removal
petitioner_arguments: The appellant had acquired a vested right to hold the office of Vice-Chancellor for the full term of five years.
The provision in s.13A is unconstitutional and void as it offends Art.14 of the Constitution
The Vice-Chancellor could not be removed by the Chancellor without any cause, without reason, without enquiry and without an opportunity being given to him to show cause against removal
respondent_arguments: No argument was presented by the respondent/defending party
court_reasoning: The Court held that the provision in s.13A is unconstitutional and void as it offends Art.14 of the Constitution
The Vice-Chancellor could not be removed by the Chancellor without any cause, without reason, without enquiry and without an opportunity being given to him to show cause against removal
holding: The Court declared that the provision in s.13A is unconstitutional and void as it offends Art.14 of the Constitution
The Vice-Chancellor was entitled to hold office for the full term of five years
